objective: Add the Gazebo sensor plugins the Revision D model lacks: an IMU and bumper contact sensor unconditionally, and the camera and depth streams behind an opt-in sensors argument, so a Gazebo run can produce the streams the perception path consumes.
decision_supported: Can the Revision D model produce sensor data at all, and does every plugin reference name a link that exists?
acceptance: The model declares an IMU and a bumper contact sensor in every expansion, because design-spec.json#/chassis/drive_sensors names both.
The three camera streams and the depth stream are declared only when the expansion is asked for them via sensors:=true, so a bare xacro expansion does not gain topics by existing.
launch/revision_d.launch.py passes sensors:=true, so a Gazebo spawn has the streams a consumer subscribes to.
Every <gazebo reference> names a link that exists; a reference to a missing link fails validate_description.py and a unit test, because Gazebo silently ignores such a reference.
Every sensor carries a system plugin; a sensor without one is refused, since it is a declaration that publishes nothing.
Sensor names are unique and every type is one of camera, depth_camera, imu, contact.
The camera field of view and the IMU covariances are marked as fixture choices rather than specification values, and a test asserts that wording stays.
The README states that a <sensor> element proves the model is able to produce data, not that a frame was published, inspected or calibrated.
README.md documents the two expansion forms and the opt-in rationale.
The existing 320 description assertions and the generated frames artifact are unchanged.
evidence: validate_description.py on a bare expansion: 338 assertions, PASS, zero sensors besides the IMU and bumper.
validate_description.py on an expansion with sensors:=true: 354 assertions, PASS, six sensors.
pytest tests/unit/test_revision_d_gazebo.py: 18 passed, 1 skipped (the pre-existing simulator skip).
The failure path: pointing a camera plugin at a link that does not exist makes validate_description.py exit 1 naming the reference, and fails test_every_gazebo_reference_names_a_real_link.
make description-check PASS with the committed frames artifact unchanged.
A full make test comparison against the unmodified main baseline showing the same pre-existing environment-blocked failures and no new ones.
stop_conditions: The change would need a sensor the design spec does not claim, such as a LiDAR the chassis does not carry.
The change would require regenerating revision-d-frames.json or moving a documented dimension; this issue changes no frame.
A write outside allowed_paths is required, especially to the frozen tabletop fixture or to the generated artifact.
Running a Gazebo acceptance case would need a simulator; the new assertions read the expanded model instead and claim no run.
data_classification: Repository-local xacro, Python and Markdown. No credentials, private data or unreviewed assets.
model_policy: Deterministic xacro expansion and pytest; no model inference and no network access added by this change.
risks_and_fallbacks: Adding sensors unconditionally would change what a plain xacro expansion declares, so a CI check would start depending on a rendering backend. The camera streams are therefore opt-in, and only the IMU and bumper, which the spec claims as hardware, are always present.
A wrong gazebo reference is silently ignored by Gazebo, which is how the model had camera frames and no camera sensors. Two checks now refuse it: validate_description.py and a unit test.

The plugin file names are Gazebo Harmonic names. A different simulator version would not find them, which surfaces as a missing stream rather than a wrong claim, and the sensors are off by default outside a Gazebo launch.
Rollback is a revert of this commit: the model returns to zero sensors. Nothing reads these sensors yet, so no consumer breaks.
